adjudicated.en: As the world was being filled by the dusk, the interior of the room with its white color as foundation would've subordinate it without a struggle, and offered to the twilight the two foreign elements held in it like would a womb, as scapegoats.

adjudicated.assessment: The clause is ungrammatical and assigns no coherent subject or object. The source imagines the white room yielding to dusk and offering up the two alien presences inside it like sacrifices.
adjudicated.remedy: Recast the sentence with the room as the subject that yields to dusk and offers up its two occupants.

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the subject and comparison, but any other time of a day uses the wrong article pattern and is not idiomatic English.
adjudicated.remedy: Use any other time of day.

adjudicated.assessment: The source says the world may perish once each day. The English mistakes the distributive count for gradual destruction piece by piece.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What if the world perishes once every day?'

adjudicated.jp: 翌日とともに蘇生され、ただ人間だけがそれを知らないのだとしたら。
adjudicated.en: What if it is reborn along with the next day, and humans alone remain unaware.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 確認するすべはない。
adjudicated.en: There are no means to make sure.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 実際の世界と、人間の認識する世界が、同じだという保証はどこにもない。
adjudicated.en: Nowhere there is proof that the world of reality and the world that humans are aware of are one and the same.
comments: Still true because Heaven(tm). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The negative locative requires inversion in this construction. The source says there is no guarantee anywhere that reality and human perception coincide.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Nowhere is there any proof...'

adjudicated.jp: なのに今、ただ保健室の小空間だけが、緋色の侵攻から免れているように思えた。
adjudicated.en: And yet, right now, the small expanse of this ordinary infirmary alone appeared to be exempt from the invasion of brilliant scarlet.
comments: That's in direct contradiction with the above. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: いつになく、世界が鮮明に見ていたからだ。
adjudicated.en: Because, unusually, I had seen the world so clearly.
comments: Should have something to do with his night eyes. Or the fact that it's currently like 9AM, so the orange isn't the growing twilight, it's the morning. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the world looked unusually vivid or clear at that moment. The English turns appearance into a completed act of seeing in past perfect.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Because the world looked unusually vivid.'

adjudicated.jp: 「……完璧な人なんて、どこにもいないじゃないですか？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "...a perfect human does not exist anywhere, am I right?"
comments: See CCB1001B -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「誰だって、どこかおかしいじゃないですか」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Everybody is strange in some ways, am I right?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「いちいち欠点や失敗を攻撃していたら、生きていけないです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Attacking every single fault and mistake one by one is not the way to live."
adjudicated.assessment: The source says people could not go on living if they attacked every flaw and failure. The English weakens that consequence into general advice about a preferable way to live.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'If we attacked every flaw and mistake, we couldn't live.'

highlights.text: is not the way to live

adjudicated.jp: 「ねえ、そうでしょう？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Well? Do you agree?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 涙のひとつも出れば、格好悪く格好がつくのだが。
adjudicated.en: If I shed but a single tear, I'll look as cool as a tool.
comments: He'd be unhip all the way to the hip. So uncool it heats up the room. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ‘Cool as a tool’ deliberately creates an English contradiction in which a supposedly cool dramatic picture also makes the speaker a tool. It shifts the source’s exact 格好悪く／格好がつく wording, but preserves the self-undercutting mechanism.
adjudicated.remedy: If revising, make the simultaneous dramatic fit and personal uncoolness more explicit.

adjudicated.jp: 不思議と、激しい情動はなりをひそめていた。
adjudicated.en: Inexplicably, the extreme emotions have fallen silent.
comments: Because of the purple above, see CCC3025. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The surrounding narration is simple past, and the source says the intense emotion had curiously gone quiet. The English present perfect breaks the narrative time frame.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'the intense emotions had fallen silent.'

adjudicated.jp: 「……一人だった俺を、部活に誘ってくれた先輩のことは、ソンケーしてるわけで」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...when I was alone, and then you invited me to club, I... respect you so much for that."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 訥々と話す俺。
adjudicated.en: Speaking in halting fragments,
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 見守る先輩。
adjudicated.en: Senpai watching over me,
comments: 見守 ｖｓ　見里... but the name had been changed, so I don't think the pun's intended. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 静かに時間がうつろう。
adjudicated.en: while hours abate in the quiet.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says time passes quietly. 'Abate' means diminish in intensity and does not describe hours moving on.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Time passes quietly.'

adjudicated.jp: 「嫌われるのは嫌だから、傷つけたくもなく」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I don't want to be disliked, so I don't want to hurt anyone either."
comments: And he's learned his lesson, soon to forget it. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source coordinates two personal fears: being disliked and hurting the addressee. The English makes the second a result of the first and broadens its object to anyone.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I don't want to be disliked, and I don't want to hurt you.'

highlights.text: so I don't want to hurt anyone

adjudicated.jp: 「……さっきのことは申し訳ないと思っていて」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...I think that what I did right then is unforgivable."
adjudicated.assessment: The source says he feels sorry or remorseful about what happened. Calling the act unforgivable intensifies the moral judgment and changes the confession's stance.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I feel terrible about what happened earlier.'

adjudicated.jp: 「でも自制する自信はなくて」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But I have no self-confidence in my self-control."
adjudicated.assessment: The doubled abstract noun phrase is an unnatural calque. The source says he lacks confidence that he can restrain himself.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'm not confident I can control myself.'

adjudicated.jp: 「どうすればいいですか？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "So what can we do?"
comments: See CCB1001B. Ouch. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Eh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「まずどこに気をつけたらいいんです？　わたしとしては」

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「怪我に気をつけろってことですね？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "So I should be careful not to get hurt?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yes."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「でもわたしはアンテナを組み立てたり、工具使ったり、怪我をする危険に面している」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But I am putting the antenna together, and using tools, so I really face the risk of injuries."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい、だから俺がそばにいない方が」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Yes, therefore, me not being near you..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぺけくんが」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But, Peke-kun..."
comments: awww she really wuves him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 遮って、言った。
adjudicated.en: Interjected, this she said:
adjudicated.assessment: The inversion is unidiomatic and leaves the participle without a clear subject. The source says she cut him off and spoke.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She cut me off and said,'

adjudicated.jp: 「力仕事を手伝ってくれるんでしょう？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Would you help me with the heavy lifting?"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a confident confirmation that he will help with the heavy work, not a tentative future request. The English weakens her decisive interruption.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You'll help me with the heavy lifting, won't you?'

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 効いた。
adjudicated.en: That worked.
comments: Misato uses SWEET TALK! It is super effective. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: じんわりと、肋骨に包まれた胸の奥を、震わせた。
adjudicated.en: Gradually, the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver.
comments: ...aqua splash? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English has number disagreement and invents a separate cage possessing ribs. The source says her words slowly made the depths of his rib-enclosed chest tremble.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Slowly, they made something deep inside my rib cage tremble.'

highlights.text: the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver

adjudicated.jp: 『いつもお一人なんですね』
adjudicated.en: 『You are always alone, are you.』
comments: CP CCA0016
adjudicated.assessment: The English tag question is malformed and punctuated as a statement. The source observes that he is always alone and seeks confirmation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You're always alone, aren't you?'

adjudicated.jp: 『一緒に、部活しませんか？』
adjudicated.en: 『Will you not have club together with me?』
comments: CP CCA0016
adjudicated.assessment: The phrase is not idiomatic English and obscures the invitation to do club activities together.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Would you like to join me in the club?'

adjudicated.jp: 心の中の語録に、一つ、加えられたその言葉は。
adjudicated.en: Those words had been added, as one quote, in the anthology deep inside my heart.
comments: He has an internal Book of Proverbs (though that's not the term). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 圧倒的にあたたかく、やわらかく、力強かった。
adjudicated.en: Overwhelmingly warm, overwhelmingly soft, overwhelmingly strong.
comments: Repetition would work well here, too bad it only exists in Japanese as emphasis. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 自分一人では解決できない悩みを、他人のたった一言が解消してしまう。
adjudicated.en: When I have worry that I cannot resolve alone, a single solitary word from another erases it.
adjudicated.assessment: The singular count noun lacks an article, and the construction needlessly turns the source's general statement into a temporal subordinate clause.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'A single word from someone else can erase a worry I cannot solve alone.'

adjudicated.jp: そのために、人は互いに通じ合いたいと思うのだった。
adjudicated.en: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that.
adjudicated.assessment: The English is syntactically incoherent and adds a first-person belief frame. The source concludes that this is why people want to understand and connect with one another.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That is why people want to connect with one another.'

highlights.text: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that

adjudicated.jp: 言葉で、体で、携帯で。
adjudicated.en: With words, with the body, with cellphones.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: ……通信で。
adjudicated.en: ...with intercommunication.
adjudicated.assessment: Intercommunication is unusually bureaucratic diction, but it denotes communication between parties and preserves the source proposition. Register preference alone does not sustain a confirmed error.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: ありとあらゆる手段で。
adjudicated.en: In every single way, with all possible means.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 触れあおうと努力できる。
adjudicated.en: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort:
adjudicated.assessment: The source says people are capable of striving to reach or touch one another. The English changes ability and continuing effort into a desire already accomplished.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'We can strive to reach one another.'

highlights.text: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort

adjudicated.jp: それが人だ。
adjudicated.en: that is a Person.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 「やっぱり組み立て、手伝ってもらうことにします」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "I knew it, I ended up needing to ask for help for the assembly."
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she has decided after all to have him help. The English recasts that choice as an externally imposed need.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I've decided to have you help me assemble it after all.'

highlights.text: I ended up needing to ask

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...yes ma'am."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 気恥ずかしい。
adjudicated.en: I feel ashamed.
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes self-conscious embarrassment or bashfulness, not moral shame. The English gives the feeling an unjustified ethical weight.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I feel bashful.'

adjudicated.jp: 先輩はにこにこと楽しそう。
adjudicated.en: Senpai smiles bright, looking like she's enjoying herself.
adjudicated.assessment: The verb requires an adverb in this construction. The source describes Senpai smiling brightly and looking pleased.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Senpai smiles brightly.'

adjudicated.jp: 曜子さんは、俺のことを強力な人間だと言った。
adjudicated.en: Youko-chan said that I make for a very strong human being.
comments: Odd -san honorific changed to usual -chan in the console version, so it was another error. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source uses the respectful adult address 'Youko-san.' The English changes it to the diminutive intimate suffix '-chan.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Youko-san.'

adjudicated.jp: そういう価値の認め方は、好きじゃない。
adjudicated.en: But I don't like the way she recognizes that value.
comments: Youko wouldn't see being human/a person as a positive. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 違う。
adjudicated.en: It's wrong.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 俺以外の人間は、えてして凄い。
adjudicated.en: Humans outside of me are so often amazing.
adjudicated.assessment: Humans outside of me is intelligible by calque, but in English it suggests people physically outside the speaker rather than people other than him.
adjudicated.remedy: Use other people or everyone but me.

adjudicated.jp: いつだってみみ先輩は、俺をいい気にさせたり手玉にとったり魅惑したりする。
adjudicated.en: Any time anywhere Mimi-senpai can make me feel pleasant and lead me by the nose and captivate me.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: そんなこと……自分ではできない。
adjudicated.en: That is something... that cannot be done on one's own.
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a first-person admission that he cannot do those things himself. The English generalizes it into an impersonal universal claim.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I could never do those things myself.'

highlights.text: cannot be done on one's own

adjudicated.jp: そばにいたい。
adjudicated.en: I want to be beside her,
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: and even then, there will be time.
comments: Life After Death. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source affirms that there is still time now. The English shifts it to a future after the previously named end point and adds 'even then,' reversing the temporal relation.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'And there is still time.'

adjudicated.jp: 「おねがいします」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It will be my pleasure."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "Hmmm."
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 頭を下げて、
adjudicated.en: With a bow of her head,
adjudicated.assessment: The source's implicit subject is the narrator, who bows his head. The English assigns the bow to Senpai and reverses the action immediately before she touches him.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I bow my head,'

adjudicated.jp: 先輩の手がぽんと置かれて、
adjudicated.en: Senpai makes her hands fall together with a pof,
adjudicated.assessment: The source says Senpai places one hand lightly on him. The English makes plural hands fall together, suggesting a clap and omitting the contact.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand comes to rest lightly on me,'

adjudicated.jp: こそばゆくて、
adjudicated.en: awkwardly,
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes a ticklish, pleasantly bashful sensation. 'Awkwardly' describes manner rather than the narrator's tactile and emotional response.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'feeling pleasantly ticklish,'

adjudicated.jp: やっと笑えて、
adjudicated.en: eventually smiling,
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the narrator was finally able to smile. The participial English omits ability and leaves the subject implicit.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I can finally smile,'

adjudicated.jp: これで、もとどおり。
adjudicated.en: and with that, she is as she was.
adjudicated.assessment: The source leaves the restored state implicit: 'With that, back to normal.' The English specifically asserts that Senpai herself is restored, despite the sequence centering the narrator and their relationship.
adjudicated.remedy: Preserve the open reference with 'And with that, everything is back to normal.'

adjudicated.jp: 涙が出るほど嬉しかった。
adjudicated.en: I was so happy I felt tears coming.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩の手が、カーテンをあける。

adjudicated.assessment: The source names a single hand. The English pluralizes it without support.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand opens the curtain.'

adjudicated.jp: 一瞬で、保健室はオレンジ色に食べられた。
adjudicated.en: In one instant the infirmary was devoured by the orange.
adjudicated.assessment: The English preserves the source's propositional content and local pragmatic function without a material addition, omission, or role reversal.
